items.content:
My French held for about nine minutes at a time and then collapsed. Twice
someone switched to English for me and I felt it as a small loss, which
I'm choosing to read as motivation.

The thing nobody tells you: it isn't the vocabulary. It's that they're
doing something different with the sentence than I am. I'm assembling;
they're already somewhere.

summary: French faltering abroad reveals a structural gap, not vocabulary
title: Notes from four days in Quebec City
